# Statistical Test: ANOVA
# Checking if there are significant differences in mean quantities sold across coffee types
coffee_types = df_pre_processed_data['Coffee Type'].unique()
data_per_coffee = [df_pre_processed_data[df_pre_processed_data['Coffee Type'] == coffee]['Quantity'] for coffee in coffee_types]

f_statistic, p_value = f_oneway(*data_per_coffee)

print(f"ANOVA F-statistic: {f_statistic}")
print(f"ANOVA p-value: {p_value}")

# If p-value < 0.05, we reject the null hypothesis 
if p_value < 0.05:
    print("There is a significant difference in mean quantities sold across coffee types.")
else:
    print("There is no significant difference in mean quantities sold across coffee types.")

ANOVA F-statistic: 0.6309842632354191
ANOVA p-value: 0.5950997661866411

def plot_bar(data, x, y, title, ylabel):
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
    sns.barplot(x=x, y=y, data=data, color="blue", edgecolor="black", errorbar=None)
    plt.title(title)
    plt.xlabel(x)
    plt.ylabel(ylabel)
    plt.show()

# Calculate the "Profit Mean" and "Total Quantity" for each Coffee Type
profit_mean_data = df_pre_processed_data.groupby('Coffee Type')['Profit'].mean().reset_index()
total_quantity_data = df_pre_processed_data.groupby('Coffee Type')['Quantity'].sum().reset_index()

# Rename the columns for clarity
profit_mean_data.rename(columns={'Profit': 'Profit Mean'}, inplace=True)
total_quantity_data.rename(columns={'Quantity': 'Total Quantity'}, inplace=True)

df_pre_processed_data['Order Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df_pre_processed_data['Order Date'])

# Calculate monthly trends for each year
monthly_trends = {}
for year in [2019, 2020, 2021]:
    df_year = df_pre_processed_data[df_pre_processed_data['Order Date'].dt.year == year]
    monthly_trend = df_year.resample('M', on='Order Date')['Quantity'].sum()
    monthly_trend.index = monthly_trend.index.month  # Set month-based index
    monthly_trends[year] = monthly_trend

# Create the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Plot lines in reverse order for correct overlapping
for year in reversed(monthly_trends.keys()):
    plt.plot(monthly_trends[year].index, monthly_trends[year].values, marker='o', label=str(year))

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Monthly Total Quantity Trend by Year (Overlapping)')
plt.xlabel('Month')
plt.ylabel('Total Quantity')

# Add legend
plt.legend()

plt.show()

from statsmodels.tsa.arima.model import ARIMA
# Here's a simple ARIMA(1,1,1) model. You can adjust the parameters based on your data.
monthly_quantity = df_pre_processed_data.resample('M', on='Order Date')['Quantity'].sum()
model = ARIMA(monthly_quantity, order=(1,1,1))
model_fit = model.fit()
forecast = model_fit.forecast(steps=24)  # Forecasting for 2 years (24 months)
future_dates = pd.date_range(start=df_pre_processed_data['Order Date'].max(), periods=24, freq='M')
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(monthly_quantity.index, monthly_quantity.values, label='Actual Quantity')
plt.plot(future_dates, forecast, label='Forecasted Average Quantity', linestyle='--')
plt.title('Quantity Forecast for the Next 2 Years')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Quantity')
plt.legend()

# 3c) What coffee type is trending each year?
# Assuming df_pre_processed_data is your DataFrame
df_pre_processed_data['Order Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df_pre_processed_data['Order Date'])

# Extract relevant features
df_pre_processed_data['Year'] = df_pre_processed_data['Order Date'].dt.year

# Group data by Year and Coffee Type, summing up the quantities
coffee_trends = df_pre_processed_data.groupby(['Year', 'Coffee Type'])['Quantity'].sum().reset_index()

# Find the coffee type with the highest quantity for each year
trending_coffee_types = coffee_trends.loc[coffee_trends.groupby('Year')['Quantity'].idxmax()]
# Plot the trending coffee types using a bar graph
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Color palette for the bars
colors = plt.cm.viridis(np.linspace(0, 1, len(trending_coffee_types['Coffee Type'].unique())))

# Bar width for each year
bar_width = 0.3  # Adjusted to be narrower

for idx, (coffee_type, data) in enumerate(trending_coffee_types.groupby('Coffee Type')):
    plt.bar(data['Year'] + idx * bar_width, data['Quantity'], width=bar_width, label=coffee_type, color=colors[idx])

plt.title('Trending Coffee Types Each Year')
plt.xlabel('Year')
plt.ylabel('Total Quantity')

# Adjusting x-axis ticks for better spacing
plt.xticks(trending_coffee_types['Year'].unique() + bar_width * (len(trending_coffee_types['Coffee Type'].unique()) - 1) / 2, labels=trending_coffee_types['Year'].unique())

plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

us_quantity = df_pre_processed_data[df_pre_processed_data['Country'] == 'United States']
max_state_name = None  # Initialize to None
max_state_quantity = None  # Initialize to None
max_customers_state = None  # Initialize to None
max_customers_count = None  # Initialize to None

if not us_quantity.empty:
    # Find state with the most quantity
    state_quantity = us_quantity.groupby('state_name')['Quantity'].sum()
    if not state_quantity.empty:
        max_state_name = state_quantity.idxmax()
        max_state_quantity = state_quantity[max_state_name]

    # Find state with the most customers
    customers_count = us_quantity['state_name'].value_counts()
    if not customers_count.empty:
        max_customers_state = customers_count.idxmax()
        max_customers_count = customers_count[max_customers_state]

    # Print the results
    if max_state_name:
        print(f"The state with the most quantity in the US is: {max_state_name} with a quantity of {max_state_quantity}")
    else:
        print("There are no quantity records for states in the US.")

    if max_customers_state:
        print(f"The state with the most customers in the US is: {max_customers_state} with {max_customers_count} customers.")

    # Relationship between Most Customers and Most Sales
    if max_state_name and max_customers_state:
        print(f"Do the state with the most customers and the state with the most quantity match? {'Yes' if max_state_name == max_customers_state else 'No'}")

else:
    print("There are no US records in the dataset.")

The state with the most quantity in the US is: Texas with a quantity of 316
The state with the most customers in the US is: California with 90 customers.
Do the state with the most customers and the state with the most quantity match? No

# List of specific countries
selected_countries = ['United States','Ireland', 'United Kingdom']

mycolors = ["#FAE4BA", "hotpink", "skyblue", "#11dc15"]
# Create subplots for each preference for each country
fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows=len(selected_countries), ncols=3, figsize=(18, 6 * len(selected_countries)))

for i, country in enumerate(selected_countries):
    # Extract relevant columns for the current country
    country_data = df_pre_processed_data[df_pre_processed_data['Country'] == country][['Coffee Type', 'Roast Type', 'Size']]
    
    # Plot coffee type preferences
    coffee_type_distribution = country_data['Coffee Type'].value_counts()
    axes[i, 0].pie(coffee_type_distribution, labels=coffee_type_distribution.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', textprops={'fontsize': 24}, startangle=90, colors=mycolors)
    axes[i, 0].set_title(f'{country} - Coffee Type Preferences')

    # Plot roast type preferences
    roast_type_distribution = country_data['Roast Type'].value_counts()
    axes[i, 1].pie(roast_type_distribution, labels=roast_type_distribution.index, autopct='%1.1f%%',textprops={'fontsize': 24},  startangle=90, colors=mycolors)
    axes[i, 1].set_title(f'{country} - Roast Type Preferences')

    # Plot size preferences
    size_distribution = country_data['Size'].value_counts()
    axes[i, 2].pie(size_distribution, labels=size_distribution.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', textprops={'fontsize': 24}, startangle=90, colors=mycolors)
    axes[i, 2].set_title(f'{country} - Size Preferences')

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Hypothesis Testing (e.g., t-test)
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

loyalty_yes = df_pre_processed_data[df_pre_processed_data['Loyalty Card'] == 'Yes']['Quantity']
loyalty_no = df_pre_processed_data[df_pre_processed_data['Loyalty Card'] == 'No']['Quantity']

t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(loyalty_yes, loyalty_no)
print(f"T-statistic: {t_stat}, P-value: {p_value}")

T-statistic: -1.3529501735561673, P-value: 0.1763779553140092
